summary: The root أبي (aby) primarily means to refuse, reject, or decline something, often with a sense of aversion or disdain.

headwords.gloss: A paucity; deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in the breast; a revulsion of the milk in the udder

parts.t: deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in the breast:
a revulsion of the milk in the udder;
(K;) but the saying “in the udder” requires consideration. (TA:) You say to a woman, when she has a fever on the occasion of childbirth,
deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in thy breast.

headwords.def: إِبْيَةٌ أب أبي أبيه أبية ابيه ابية آبي آبيه آبية A paucity, or deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in the breast: (Fr, TS:) or a revulsion of the milk in the udder; (K;) but the saying “in the udder” requires consideration. (TA:) You say to a woman, when she has a fever on the occasion of childbirth, إِنَّمَا هذِهِ الحُمَّى إِبْيَةٌ ثَدْيِكَ [ This fever is only occasioned by the paucity, or deficiency, and revulsion, of the milk in thy breast. ] (TA.)
أَبْيَانٌ and أَبْيَانُ and أَبَيَانٌ : see آبٍ , in four places.

headwords.def: أَبِىٌّ and أَبِيَةٌ : see آبٍ , in three places. Also, the former ( أَبِىٌّ ), She [app. a camel, or any beast,] that refuses, or refrains from, fodder, by reason of her suffering from indigestion: and she that refuses, or refrains from, the stallion, by reason of her having little appetency. (AA.) [See also أَوَابٍ , voce آبٍ .]
